questions.question: How do I change the address on my driving licence?
key_facts: It does not cost anything to change your address with DVLA
You can apply online (or by post)

questions.question: How much does it cost to renew my driving licence when I turn 70?
key_facts: Renewing a licence at 70 or over is free
You must renew every 3 years after reaching 70

questions.question: How old do I have to be to apply for a provisional driving licence?
key_facts: You must be at least 15 years and 9 months old
It costs £34 to apply online

questions.question: How much does it cost to replace a stolen driving licence?
key_facts: A replacement licence costs £20 online
You should contact the police if it was stolen

questions.question: How long do penalty points stay on my licence?
key_facts: Penalty points/endorsements stay on your driving record for 4 or 11 years, depending on the offence

questions.question: How much does the car theory test cost?
key_facts: The car theory test costs £23

questions.question: How do I tell DVLA my car is off the road?
key_facts: Tell DVLA online (or by phone/post) that the vehicle is off the road: a SORN
You get a refund for any full months of remaining tax

questions.question: Can I get a refund on my vehicle tax if I sell my car?
key_facts: You cancel vehicle tax by telling DVLA you sold or transferred the vehicle; there is no other way to cancel
You get a refund for any full months of remaining tax

questions.question: Which vehicles are exempt from vehicle tax?
key_facts: Exempt vehicles include historic vehicles made before 1 January 1986 and vehicles used by a disabled person (other examples: mobility vehicles, mowing machines, steam vehicles, agricultural vehicles)
Electric cars are no longer exempt: from 1 April 2025 they must pay vehicle tax

questions.question: How do I check the MOT history of a car?
key_facts: You need the vehicle's number plate (registration number)
The history shows past pass/fail results, recorded mileage and when the next MOT is due

questions.question: How early can I get my MOT without losing my renewal date?
key_facts: You can get an MOT up to a month (minus a day) before it runs out and keep the same renewal date

questions.question: What do I need to do when I sell my car?
key_facts: Tell DVLA you've sold or transferred the vehicle (online, or by post if there is no log book)
Your vehicle tax is cancelled and you get a refund for any full months left

questions.question: How do I change the address on my V5C log book?
key_facts: You can change the address online as the registered keeper, or by post
It is usually free to update your V5C

questions.question: What should I do if my car has been stolen?
key_facts: Tell the police (dial 101) and your insurance company straight away
If the insurer pays out, you must tell DVLA the vehicle has been sold to the insurer

questions.question: What are the penalties for speeding?
key_facts: The minimum penalty is a £100 fine and 3 penalty points
You could be disqualified if you reach 12 or more points within 3 years

questions.question: How do I get my licence back after a driving ban?
key_facts: You must apply for a new licence to drive again
For drink or drug driving you can reapply before the disqualification ends, using the D27 form DVLA sends

questions.question: Can I drive if I have diabetes?
key_facts: You must tell DVLA if your insulin treatment lasts (or will last) over 3 months
You do not need to tell DVLA if the diabetes is treated by diet alone

questions.question: What are the eyesight rules for driving?
key_facts: You must be able to read a number plate from 20 metres away
Minimum visual acuity of decimal 0.5 (6/12) on the Snellen scale, with glasses or contact lenses if needed

questions.question: How do I change the photo on my driving licence?
key_facts: It costs £14 to change the photo online
You do this by renewing your licence (online, or by post for £17)

questions.question: What do the codes on my driving licence mean?
key_facts: The codes on the back of the licence set conditions you must meet to drive
Examples: 01 eyesight correction (glasses or contact lenses); 78 automatic transmission only

questions.question: How do I swap my paper driving licence for a photocard?
key_facts: You only have to exchange a paper licence if you change your address or name, want to do Driver CPC training, or it is defaced, lost, stolen or destroyed
It is free if you changed name or address and still have the paper licence; otherwise £20

questions.question: How much does the driving test cost?
key_facts: The car driving test costs £62 on weekdays
It costs £75 on evenings, weekends and bank holidays

questions.question: How do I change my driving test appointment?
key_facts: You can change a car driving test only 2 times
You must change it yourself; your instructor is not allowed to

questions.question: How do I tax a car if I haven't received a tax reminder?
key_facts: You can tax online with the 11-digit reference number from your V5C (or the 12-digit number on the green new keeper slip)
You can also tax by phone or at a Post Office

questions.question: I've just bought a used car. What do I need to do to tax it and get it registered in my name?
key_facts: You must tax the vehicle before you can use it on the road
The seller usually registers a used vehicle for you (online or by post) and gives you the green 'new keeper' slip
You can tax it using the reference number from the green new keeper slip (or the V5C if it is already in your name)

questions.question: I'm moving house. Which of my licence and vehicle records do I need to update?
key_facts: Change the address on your driving licence
Change the address on your vehicle log book (V5C) and your vehicle tax Direct Debit, if you pay that way

questions.question: My car is over 40 years old. Does it need an MOT, and does it need vehicle tax?
key_facts: No MOT is needed if the vehicle was built or first registered more than 40 years ago and has had no substantial changes
Vehicles built before 1 January 1986 are exempt from vehicle tax, but you must still tax the vehicle (apply for the exemption)

questions.question: I'm 17 and want to learn to drive. What licence and tests do I need, and what do they cost?
key_facts: You can apply for a provisional licence from 15 years and 9 months (£34 online)
You must pass a theory test (£23) and a driving test (£62 weekdays)
You can usually start driving a car at 17

questions.question: My car has been written off. What do I tell DVLA and what happens to my vehicle tax?
key_facts: You must tell DVLA the vehicle was written off and scrapped by your insurer (you can be fined £1,000 if not)
You get a vehicle tax refund for any full months left

questions.question: I'm over 70 and have a medical condition. How do I renew my driving licence?
key_facts: You can renew free online from 70 if you meet the eyesight requirement and nothing prevents you from driving
You must tell DVLA about medical conditions that affect your driving (fine of up to £1,000 if not)

How many times can I change my car driving test booking now?
key_facts: You can only make 2 changes to a car driving test booking (it was 6 before 31 March 2026)

questions.question: Can my driving instructor book or cancel my driving test for me?
key_facts: Since 12 May 2026 only the learner can book, change or cancel their own car driving test; instructors are not allowed to

questions.question: If I want to move my driving test to a different test centre, where can I move it to?
key_facts: You can only move your test to one of the 3 nearest test centres to where it is booked (since 9 June 2026), or back to the centre you first booked

questions.question: The mileage on my MOT record is wrong. How do I get it corrected?
key_facts: Report it online (if the MOT was more than 28 days ago); within 28 days ask the MOT centre
You must upload evidence of the correct mileage, e.g. an invoice, emissions printout, service receipt or job card, dated within one day of the MOT

questions.question: How do I set up a Direct Debit to pay my vehicle tax?
key_facts: Set it up when you tax your vehicle online or at a Post Office
You need your address, date of birth and bank or building society name, account number and sort code
There is a 5% surcharge for paying monthly or every 6 months, none for yearly
